messages:
mike: Hey team — noticed a regression on dashboards after last night's deploy, charts are stuttering and some long-tail requests are timing out :bug:

lina: saw that too. Which routes are affected? heatline + timeseries widgets? :eyes:

mike: mainly the multi-series panels. CPU looks fine but main bundle parse time jumped. Telemetry shows a big spike in `main.bundle.js` parse and rehydrate.

lina: can you paste the bundle size diff?

mike: sure — ran a quick size check:
```
$ ls -lh dist/main*.js
-rw-r--r-- 1 build 4.2M main.bundle.js  # was 3.85M yesterday
-rw-r--r-- 1 build 6.1M vendor.bundle.js
# build step added ~350KB to main.bundle.js after telemetry-proxy change
```

tom: telemetry-proxy change? that landed in the infra canary at 02:15 UTC. It added a tiny instrumentation lib for sampling.

ashley: product noticed slow dashboard load times from some EU users this morning, pinged support.

lina: the interesting bit: network waterfall shows more small blocking requests during render, likely because prefix KV cache misses cause extra XHRs. routing-policy change last week bumped prefetch priority down for many dashboards.

mike: here's a stack from client devtools when the freeze happens:
```
UnhandledRangeError: invalid decode at renderSeries (main.bundle.js:115432)
    at hydrate (main.bundle.js:115510)
    at startRender (main.bundle.js:115680)
    at onData (charts.ts:382)
```

mike: not sure if the decode error is symptom or cause but parse+hydrate spike coincides with more KV fallback hits from EU region.

tom: quick note from infra-bot: canary deploy 2024-05-10T02:15 by @tom. change: telemetry sampling lib v1.2.0 added `compact-sample` module.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary status: healthy 30m, cpu 12%, mem 48% — no infra alarms.

lina: suggests: 1) temporarily revert sampling module on canary 2) repro locally with sourcemap and `--max_old_space_size` to check parse 3) check prefetch routing/quota policy that lowered prefetch priority.

mike: +1 to repro. I can repro in local chrome emulation by throttling CPU to 4x and hitting the same dashboard. parse time jumps from ~420ms to ~1.1s.

ashley: if revert is needed, can we gate by EU region only to limit blast radius? customers impacted are mostly EU.

tom: we can rollback the canary for EU edge pool and keep global canary. rolling back EU now would take ~7m.

lina: also curious if tree-shaking broke — maybe `compact-sample` pulled in a dependency that disables a module-level lazy import. can someone run `webpack-bundle-analyzer` on the build?

mike: running analyzer now, will share screenshot in thread.

mike: quick workaround: enabling client-side chunking for charts reduces main parse by offloading heavy render code to worker. but that is a one-off change and risks new edge cases.

tom: routing/quota angle: earlier change reduced prefetch QPS for non-enterprise routes. that increases cold loads which exacerbate parse stalls. if we temporarily bump prefetch quota for dashboard routes we should see fewer cold requests.

infra-bot: perf-monitor: heatline_series_render_latency p99 jumped from 210ms -> 1.3s at 02:22 UTC correlated with canary.

lina: plan suggestion: A) revert telemetry sampling in EU canary B) bump prefetch quota for dashboards for 2 hours C) run canary perf tests with CPU throttle and compare p95/p99.

ashley: agree with plan A+B. I'm opening an incident page for external comms.

mike: I'll prepare a minimal revert PR now and add a smoke test that runs the `sourcemap-explorer` check in CI.

lina: I'll run analyzer and confirm if any unexpected deps landed.

tom: I'll bump prefetch quota for the dashboard routing policy to normal and monitor.

deploy-bot: [action] Created PR #4123 revert(telemetry-sampling): remove compact-sample import — by mike.

mike: thx — will request review from @lina.

lina: quick note: if revert fixes perf we should then do a narrower follow-up to reintroduce sampling with lazy load and ensure it doesn't pull big deps into main bundle.

ashley: timeline pls — we should have EU rollback and prefetch bump within the hour. status updates in this thread only. :shipit:

mike: rolling EU canary back now (starting 02:58 UTC). will report when done.

infra-bot: Canary rollback started for EU pool.

mike: rollback complete. initial heatline p99 back to ~240ms. seems promising.

tom: prefetch quota bumped. monitoring p95/p99.

infra-bot: perf-monitor: heatline_series_render_latency p99 reduced to 260ms after rollback and quota bump.

lina: looks like combo fixed it. follow-up items: smaller sampling bundle as a lazy import, add perf gate to canary before rollouts, and add KV cache telemetry for region misses.

mike: opened perf ticket PERF-2374 with notes + repro steps. assigning to eng-platform.

ashley: thanks all. closing loop once the lazy-import fix lands. :white_check_mark:
